issue_context.body:
## The problem

I set up netatmo like described in https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/netatmo/ in the following steps:

* no netatmo extension was configured
* add entries in configuration.yaml
* restart hass
* on hass got to settings - integrations and add netatmo extension
* select "configuration.yaml" 
* restart hass

Until restart all was ok and netatmo says it is configured. But wenn home assistant starts, the exception "Error while setting up netatmo platform for sensor" is thrown and netatmo does not detect my devices.


## Environment

Home assistant Version: 0.111.4 running in docker with following docker-compose.yml

```yml
version: '2'
services:
    mqtt:
        container_name: mqtt
        image: eclipse-mosquitto:1.5.4
        restart: always
        ports: 
            - 1883:1883
            - 9001
    hassdb:
        container_name: hassdb
        image: mysql
        command: mysqld --default-authentication-plugin=mysql_native_password 
        restart: always
        ports:
            - 3306:3306
        environment:
            MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: 'xxx' 
            MYSQL_DATABASE: 'homeassistant'
            MYSQL_USER: 'hass'
            MYSQL_PASSWORD: 'xxx' 
    homeassistant:
        depends_on:
            - hassdb
            - mqtt
        restart: always
        container_name: hass
        image: homeassistant/home-assistant
        volumes:
            - ./hass-config:/config
            - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
        ports:
            - 8123:8123
```

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
netatmo:
  client_id: myclientid
  client_secret: mysecret
```

review_comments: Can we get rid of the dispatcher here?
As discussed on Discord, this wont be changed easily and can be left for a future PR.
We can use `self._async_current_entries`.
Debug level.
We can invert this check and append and return if true. Then we can outdent below.
This isn't needed anymore.

Any time we get `RESULT_TYPE_CREATE_ENTRY `, we should mock out async_setup and async_create_entry so we don't unexpectedly setup and start doing I/O

```
    with patch(
        "homeassistant.components.netatmo.async_setup", return_value=True
    ) as mock_setup, patch(
        "homeassistant.components.netatmo.async_setup_entry", return_value=True,
    ) as mock_setup_entry:
```
...

```
    assert len(mock_setup.mock_calls) == 1
    assert len(mock_setup_entry.mock_calls) == 1
```
Disregard, I missed that this was an options flow 👍
As above.
Why are we using the event bus for integration internal communication? We normally use the dispatch helper when we need to signal different parts of the integration.
`netatmo_event` is the webhook event that is just reused here to improve responsibility of the integration in case the webhook is active.
Is this a pattern that we use in other integrations?
Not that I am aware of but I haven't researched it much.

If this is not an established pattern for webhook integrations, I'd say we should not reuse this event internally and keep it for other users only. The internal communication should go via dispatch helper signal.

Maybe I misunderstood your question but webhook events are handled on the event bus elsewhere, for example `mobile_app`. I thought you were talking about listening on the event bus for such event, which made sense to me to be reused here.

Yes, I'm talking about listening for this event. The event bus should normally not be used for internal communication within an integration. Our dispatch helper is the replacement that have similar features that we can use instead.
Is if forbidden to listen for that even at all then? Or can I listen for it in the data handler and communicate the events to the individual platform?

In the webhook event handler, we'll do two things:

1. Fire an event bus event with the event data, using `hass.bus.async_fire`.
2. Dispatch the event data to the platforms with the dispatch helper, ie using `async_dispatcher_send`.
Ok, that's fine with me.
There's no await inside this coroutine so it could be a `callback` instead. Decorate it with `@callback` imported from core.py.
Same here
Oops
Why are we creating a new entry when updating options? That sounds weird. Maybe this method just needs to be renamed?
I'll try to come up with a better name.
It looks like we hold an entire copy of the device registry in memory here at the time this is setup.  Can we get these another way ?
Well, yeah, actually I only need the name and id. Fixed that.
What line can raise here? This try... except block looks bigger than neeed. We want that scope to be as small as possible.
Please separate words with underscore in variable and function names.

If we pass a dict when registering the entity service, the helper will create an entity id schema by default.

https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/dev_101_services#entity-services
